name: Trilobita DocVault
author: trilobita

sections.description:
Trilobita DocVault turns WordPress into a document library. Upload a file once and its download link never changes: when you upload a new version, every link on your pages, menus and emails serves the new file automatically. Visitors find documents in a searchable, sortable table, and you keep a version history for every file.

Key Features:

  • Version History – Upload a new version and the download link stays the same. Download, restore or delete earlier versions (up to 5 per document), with optional version notes.
  • Searchable Document Library – The [trdv_list] shortcode shows a responsive table with live search, sortable columns and pagination, plus optional category, tag and file type filters.
  • View in Browser – PDFs get a View button so visitors can read them without downloading.
  • Document List Block – Add a searchable list of documents to any page in the block editor, for example every document in a category (such as the papers for one meeting), and choose the sorting, columns and filters in the block settings.
  • Document Block – Add a single document to any page or post in the block editor, with Full and Minimal layouts.
  • Inline Download Links – Link any text to a document from the block editor toolbar, or with the [trdv_link] shortcode.
  • Access Control – Make documents public or available to logged-in users only, as a site-wide default or per document.
  • Protected Files – Files are served only through DocVault’s download links, which check access first. Direct access to the upload folder is blocked on Apache, and Site Health warns you if your server (for example Nginx) needs a rule.
  • Expiry Dates – Set an optional expiry date and the document is hidden automatically once it passes.
  • Download Tracking – See download counts in the admin list, and optionally show them on the frontend.
  • Drag & Drop Upload – Drop a file to upload it; the title is filled in from the file name.
  • Categories and Tags – Organise documents with their own categories (or share your post categories) and tags.
  • Manual Sort Order – Drag documents into your preferred order and use [trdv_list orderby="menu_order"] to show that order on the frontend.
  • Site Search – Documents appear in your site’s search results (can be turned off).
  • Privacy Tools – Works with the WordPress personal data export and erasure tools.
  • File Types – PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, PPT, PPTX, ODT, ODS, ODP, RTF, CSV and TXT.

If DocVault is useful to you, please consider leaving a review. It helps other people find the plugin.

Switching from another download plugin?

If your site uses WordPress Download Manager or Download Monitor, the free Trilobita DocVault Migrator copies your downloads into DocVault, with a dry run first and rollback if you change your mind. Old download links and shortcodes keep working without editing your pages. WordPress Download Manager and Download Monitor are third-party plugins, not affiliated with Trilobita.

Go further with Trilobita DocVault Pro

Trilobita DocVault Pro adds enterprise-grade features for teams that need more control:

  • Unlimited Version History – Remove the 5-version limit, with optional per-document limits and automatic pruning of old versions.
  • Per-Document Access Control – Restrict individual documents to specific user roles.
  • Audit Trail – Full activity log with CSV export for compliance and accountability.
  • Email Notifications – Configurable alerts for uploads, updates, and approvals.
  • Document Approval Workflow – Require documents to be reviewed before publishing.
  • Bulk Upload – Upload multiple documents at once with duplicate detection.
  • Download Analytics – Detailed per-version download statistics.
  • Duplicate Detection – Find and merge duplicate documents to save storage.
  • Storage Management – Advanced tools for monitoring and cleaning up storage.
  • Card and Button Layouts – Two extra layouts for the Document block.
  • More File Types – Allow images (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP), ZIP, AI and EPS files.
  • Button Colours – Match download buttons to your brand.

Privacy

Trilobita DocVault stores the following user data:

  • Uploader user ID – Stored as post meta (_trdv_uploaded_by) to track who uploaded each document version.
  • Download logs – Each download is recorded with the downloader’s IP address, browser user agent, user ID (if logged in) and the time, in a custom database table (trdv_download_log).

This data is handled in compliance with GDPR and CCPA:

  • The plugin registers with the WordPress privacy tools for data export and erasure requests.
  • Suggested privacy policy text is added to the WordPress Privacy Policy Guide (Settings > Privacy).
  • Download logs for registered users can be exported and erased with the WordPress personal data tools. Downloads by visitors who are not logged in are not linked to an email address, so they cannot be matched by these tools.

Usage

Document Block (Gutenberg):

Add a single document with a download button directly in the block editor:

  1. Click the + button to add a block
  2. Search for “DocVault Document”
  3. Under Select Document, type part of the title and choose the document

Block options:

  • Layout: Full (with icon and download button) or Minimal (compact inline link)
  • Show/hide file icon (full layout only)
  • Show/hide file info (type and size; a file type badge in the minimal layout)
  • Show/hide view button (PDF and images, full layout only)
  • Show/hide description (full layout only)
  • Show/hide download count (full layout only)
  • Alignment (left, center, right, wide)

Document List Block (Gutenberg):

Add a searchable, sortable table of documents in the block editor:

  1. Click the + button to add a block
  2. Search for “DocVault Document List”
  3. In the block settings, choose the categories and tags to list (none selected lists all documents)

Block settings:

  • Documents: categories, tags and file type. Documents in any selected category (including subcategories) that also have any selected tag are listed
  • Sorting: sort by date published, title, manual order, file size, file type or downloads; ascending or descending; documents per page (up to 100)
  • Display: search box, category, tag and file type filters, view and download buttons, download count, and columns
  • Alignment (wide, full)

The block shows the same table as the [trdv_list] shortcode, with the same access control: visitors only see documents they are allowed to access. Categories and tags are saved by ID, so renaming one does not break the block. If every selected category or tag is deleted, the block shows nothing rather than all documents.

[trdv_list] — Document Table Shortcode:

Display a searchable, sortable table of documents on any page or post:

[trdv_list]

Parameters:

  • category – Filter by document category slug, or several slugs separated by commas (documents in any of them)
  • tag – Filter by document tag slug, or several slugs separated by commas (documents in any of them)
  • include – Show only these documents: document IDs separated by commas (up to 100). Combined with the other filters
  • type – Filter by file type (pdf, docx, etc.)
  • orderby – Sort by: date (publish date), title, size, type, downloads, menu_order (default: date). Use menu_order to display documents in the drag-and-drop order set in the admin list. When menu_order is selected and order is not explicitly set, the list defaults to ASC.
  • order – ASC or DESC (default: DESC)
  • show_search – Show search box: true/false (default: true)
  • show_download – Show download button: true/false (default: true)
  • show_view – Show view button for PDFs and images: true/false (default: true)
  • show_category_filter – Show category dropdown filter: true/false (default: false)
  • show_tag_filter – Show tag dropdown filter: true/false (default: false)
  • show_type_filter – Show file type dropdown filter (only types present in the library): true/false (default: false)
  • show_count – Show download count column: true/false (default: false)
  • columns – Columns to display: title, type, size, date (default: title,type,size,date)
  • per_page – Documents per page (default: 20, maximum 100). Use -1 for the maximum
  • show_expired – Include expired documents: true/false (default: false)

Examples:

[trdv_list type="pdf" orderby="title" order="ASC"]
[trdv_list category="reports" show_search="false" columns="title,date"]
[trdv_list orderby="menu_order"]
[trdv_list show_category_filter="true" show_type_filter="true" show_count="true"]
[trdv_list show_tag_filter="true"]
[trdv_list show_download="false" show_view="true"]

Document Link Toolbar Button:

Link any selected text to a document download without leaving the block editor:

  1. Select the text you want to turn into a download link
  2. Click the document icon in the formatting toolbar (“Trilobita DocVault Link”)
  3. Choose a document from the dropdown and click Apply

[trdv_link] — Inline Document Link Shortcode:

Insert a download link within any text:

[trdv_link id="123"]Download the report[/trdv_link]

Parameters:

  • id (required) – The document ID
  • new_tab – Open in new tab: true/false (default: false)
  • class – Add custom CSS class

Examples:

[trdv_link id="123"] - Uses document title as link text
[trdv_link id="123"]Click here[/trdv_link] - Custom link text
[trdv_link id="123" new_tab="true"]Download[/trdv_link] - Opens in new tab
sections.installation:
From the WordPress plugin directory (recommended):

  1. Go to Plugins > Add New in your WordPress admin.
  2. Search for “Trilobita DocVault”.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  4. Go to the new Documents menu in the admin sidebar. A short getting-started guide walks you through uploading your first document and creating a documents page.

Manual installation:

  1. Upload the trilobita-docvault folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to the new Documents menu in the admin sidebar. A short getting-started guide walks you through uploading your first document and creating a documents page.
sections.faq:
What file types are supported?

Trilobita DocVault supports PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, PPT, PPTX, ODT, ODS, ODP, RTF, CSV, and TXT files.

How does version control work?

From the Edit Document screen, you can upload new versions of a file. The plugin keeps a full version history with the ability to download, restore, or delete any previous version. By default, up to 5 versions per document are kept.

How do I display documents on the frontend?

There are four ways:

  1. DocVault Document List block — a searchable, sortable table of documents, set up in the block editor sidebar: pick categories and tags, sorting, columns and filters.
  2. [trdv_list] shortcode — the same table, for the Classic Editor, widgets or page builders. On a new site, the getting-started guide’s Create a documents page button sets up a draft page with this table for you.
  3. DocVault Document block — add a single document with a download button directly in the Gutenberg block editor.
  4. [trdv_link] shortcode — inserts an inline download link within any text. You can also use the Trilobita DocVault Link toolbar button in the block editor to link selected text to a document without using a shortcode.

How do I group documents, for example the papers for a meeting?

Use a category for each group. For committee meetings, for example, create a “Committee meetings” category with a subcategory per meeting, and put the agenda, reports and minutes for each meeting in its subcategory. A document can be in several categories, so the minutes can also go in a “Minutes” category.

Then add a DocVault Document List block to a page and choose the category in the block settings. A parent category also lists the documents in its subcategories. Each document keeps its own download link and version history, so a corrected report replaces the old one everywhere it is listed.

Are download links secure?

Yes. Download links use the format /trdv/download/{id}/ rather than a direct path to the file. Every download request is handled by WordPress, which checks access permissions before serving the file. The actual file location on the server is never exposed. Restricted documents cannot be accessed by guessing a URL, and files are always forced to download rather than opened inline in the browser (except PDFs and images opened with the View button).

On Apache, DocVault blocks direct web access to its upload folder with an .htaccess file, so stored files can only be reached through these download links. Nginx and some other servers ignore .htaccess files, so on those servers you should add an equivalent rule to your server configuration. DocVault checks this for you: go to Tools > Site Health, and if stored files can be downloaded directly you will see a warning with the exact rule for your site. For Nginx:

location ^~ /wp-content/uploads/trdv-documents/ { deny all; }

If your site has a legacy sdm-documents folder from an early version of the plugin, add the same rule for that folder too.

Can I restrict document access?

Yes. In Documents > Settings, set the default access to Public or Logged-in users only. Each document can override the default in its Access Control box. Restricting documents to specific user roles is available in DocVault Pro.

Where are uploaded files stored?

Files are stored in /wp-content/uploads/trdv-documents/. By default all files are kept in one folder; in Documents > Settings you can choose folders by document ID or by year and month instead.

Can I replace a document without breaking links?

Yes. Open the document, drop the new file into Upload New Version and click Update. Download links point to the document, not the file, so every existing link now serves the new version. The previous file stays in the version history.

Can I count downloads?

Yes. Every download through a DocVault link is counted. Counts appear in the admin document list and on each document’s edit screen, and you can show them on the frontend with [trdv_list show_count="true"] or the Document block’s Show download count option.

How many versions are kept?

By default, up to 5 versions per document are kept. Older versions are automatically removed when the limit is reached.

Can I set an expiry date on a document?

Yes. Each document has an optional expiry date field in the admin. Once the date passes, the document is automatically hidden from all frontend listings — the [trdv_list] shortcode, AJAX search, Query Loop block, and REST API. Direct download and view URLs are also blocked for non-admin, non-author users. To include expired documents in a specific [trdv_list] listing, use [trdv_list show_expired="true"]. Admins and the document’s author can still download expired documents directly; they remain visible and manageable in the admin.

Is the plugin translation-ready?

Yes, Trilobita DocVault is fully translatable. A .pot template file is included in the plugin’s languages/ folder to help you get started. Translation files should be named trilobita-docvault-{locale}.mo (e.g. trilobita-docvault-fr_FR.mo) and can be placed either in the plugin’s own languages/ folder or in /wp-content/languages/plugins/.
sections.changelog:
1.7.0

  • New: DocVault Document List block. Add a searchable, sortable list of documents to any page in the block editor, for example every document in a category, and choose categories, tags, file type, sorting, columns and filters in the block settings. Visitors only see the documents they are allowed to access, as with [trdv_list].
  • New: If your site has content from WordPress Download Manager or Download Monitor that has not been migrated, administrators see a dismissible notice about the free DocVault Migrator plugin, which imports it into DocVault.
  • Change: The Date column in document lists now shows the document’s publish date, the date the list sorts by. Previously it showed when the current file was uploaded, so uploading a new version changed the date shown without moving the document in the list.
  • Change: Documents are not included in WordPress 7.2’s random content links (/random/), which would otherwise start the download of a random document.
  • Fix: Deleting an old version, or the version limit removing the oldest one, no longer deletes a file that a later version still uses. This happened after restoring a version: the restored version shares the original’s file.
  • Fix: The DocVault blocks in the block editor now use your site’s language when a translation is available.
  • Fix: Documents sharing the same date (or other sort value) could appear in a different order on each page load, so moving between pages could repeat some documents and skip others.
  • Fix: In document lists, only columns that can be sorted can be clicked. Clicking a column added by an extension, such as DocVault Pro’s Version column, re-sorted the list by date.
  • Developer: New trdv_render_list action and trdv_document_list_block_atts filter, and the trdv.documentList.inspectorPanels JavaScript filter for adding settings to the Document List block.

1.6.1

  • New: [trdv_list include="12,34"] shows only the listed documents (document IDs, up to 100), and works with search, sorting and the other filters.
  • Fix: [trdv_list per_page="-1"] showed one document per page. A negative value now shows the maximum of 100 per page, as in WordPress.
  • New: Download Monitor’s [downloads] shortcode keeps working after migration with DocVault Migrator 1.12.0 or later, including include="..." lists. Filters DocVault cannot reproduce (for example exclude or featured="true") show nothing to visitors and a short note to editors, rather than a longer list.
  • Improvement: Compatibility rules written by DocVault Migrator are checked more strictly: a rule with a setting this version does not understand is skipped instead of partly applied.

1.6.0

  • New: Content migrated from WordPress Download Manager keeps working without editing your pages. Its download links and package shortcodes now point to the migrated documents, its listing shortcodes show the migrated categories and tags, and old download, package, category and tag URLs redirect to DocVault. Unsupported WPDM shortcodes show nothing to visitors and a short note to editors. Requires migration with DocVault Migrator 1.11.0 or later, a separate free plugin.
  • New: The document list’s category and tag options accept several slugs separated by commas.
  • Security: Documents created without an author (for example with WP-CLI or an import tool) no longer bypass their access setting and expiry date for logged-out visitors.
  • Security: Expiry dates now follow your site’s time zone everywhere. Previously downloads used UTC, so on sites ahead of UTC an expired document could still be downloaded for a few hours after its expiry date ended.
  • Fix: Permanently deleting a document now also deletes its download history (moving it to the Trash keeps it). Download history left by documents deleted earlier is removed when you update.
  • Fix: Document category and tag pages listed no documents when “Include documents in site search” was turned off.
  • Improvement: If DocVault uses WordPress categories, category pages now list documents as well as posts. Visitors only see the documents they are allowed to access.
  • Fix: A Query Loop showing posts and documents together could hide the posts from visitors when documents are restricted to logged-in users.

1.5.10

  • Fix: The document list’s search, filters, sorting and pagination keep working on sites that use page caching. Previously a cached page could carry an expired security token, and these stopped working for logged-out visitors after 12–24 hours.
  • Improvement: If a document search fails, a short message now asks the visitor to reload the page, instead of nothing happening.
  • Fix: Clicking a column heading in the document list a second time now reverses the sort order, and the sorted column shows its arrow.
  • Fix: Sorting the document list by Type now sorts by file type (it sorted by date), and sorting by Size no longer leaves out documents without a recorded size.
  • New: The Downloads column in the document list can be sorted, and [trdv_list] accepts orderby="type" and orderby="downloads".

1.5.9

  • Security: Documents restricted to logged-in users or specific roles, and expired documents, no longer appear in site search results or on document category and tag pages for visitors who cannot access them. Previously their titles and descriptions could be listed there (downloads were always blocked).
  • Security: Choosing “Specific roles” without selecting any roles now saves “Logged-in users only” with a warning, since that is how it behaved. Saved role settings are no longer cleared when the settings page is saved without DocVault Pro.
  • Security: Several hardening fixes: uploads must belong to a document, the document list is limited to 100 documents per page, downloads are marked private so shared caches never store them, legacy files are checked to be inside the DocVault folders, unknown access settings now deny access, and sort-order changes only affect documents you can edit.
  • Fix: The expiry date help text now describes the current behaviour.
  • Improvement: The Plugins screen now has a Settings link and Docs, Support and review links for DocVault, and the plugin description matches the WordPress.org listing.
  • New: Getting-started guide for new sites. While there are no documents, the Documents screen shows three short steps (upload a document, show documents on a page, choose who can see them), and the Plugins screen shows a short dismissible notice. The guide hides itself once you are set up, or you can hide it at any time. Sites that already have documents are not shown it.
  • New: “Create a documents page” button that creates a draft page containing the searchable document list and opens it in the editor for you to review and publish.
  • Improvement: The review prompt is no longer shown on sites without any documents, or while the file protection warning or the getting-started guide is showing.

1.5.8

  • Security: The Document block no longer shows restricted or expired documents when page content is rendered through admin-ajax.php (for example by a theme’s “load more” feature) for visitors who cannot access them.
  • Developer: The Document block’s Layout control and display toggles can now be extended by other plugins through the trdv.document.layoutOptions and trdv.document.layoutControls JavaScript filters. DocVault Pro 1.5.4 uses these to add its Card and Button layouts to the same Layout control, fixing a duplicate Layout control and missing toggles in the block sidebar when Pro is active. No change for sites without Pro.

1.5.7

  • Fix: Download counts are no longer lost when the same document is downloaded several times at once. The total is now updated in a single database operation.
  • Fix: Saving a document no longer reports an expiry date change unless the expiry date actually changed. Previously every save of a document without an expiry date was reported as “cleared”, which created misleading entries in the DocVault Pro audit log.
  • Fix: The Upload Date column in the admin document list and the Date column in the [trdv_list] table now show your site’s time zone instead of UTC.

1.5.6

  • Security: Direct web access to the DocVault upload folder is now blocked on Apache servers. Previously, a stored file could be downloaded straight from its storage URL, bypassing access restrictions and expiry dates. Existing sites are protected automatically on upgrade. Nginx users should add the server rule described in the FAQ.
  • Security: New Site Health check that tests whether stored document files can be downloaded directly. If they can (for example on Nginx without the server rule), Site Health and the DocVault admin screens show a warning with the exact rule to add.
  • Improvement: The review prompt can now also appear once you have added 5 or more documents (and have used DocVault for at least 7 days), in addition to the existing 21-day prompt. Whichever comes first is shown; dismissing or snoozing it applies to both.

1.5.5

  • Compatibility: Confirmed compatible with WordPress 7.1.
  • Fix: Document block editor styles now declared via style_handles so they load correctly inside the always-iframed post editor introduced in WordPress 7.1, instead of relying on a WordPress core compatibility fallback.

1.5.4

  • Improvement: The Document block’s document picker is now a live search field backed by the REST API, replacing the static dropdown that was silently limited to 100 documents.

1.5.3

  • Fix: Download and View buttons in the document list no longer wrap their label across two lines.

1.5.2

  • Fix: Admin CSS accent colours now use var(--wp-admin-theme-color) so buttons, borders, and links match whichever admin colour scheme is active (Fresh, Modern, Ocean, etc.).

1.5.1

  • Docs: corrected expiry date FAQ — expired documents are now blocked at download, view, and REST level for non-admin/non-author users (enforced since 1.4.9; FAQ previously described the old behaviour).
  • Docs: corrected stale line number in phpcs:disable comment in class-admin-interface.php.

1.5.0

  • Compatibility: Confirmed compatible with WordPress 7.0.
  • Enhancement: Block API version updated to 3, enabling iframed post editor support in WordPress 7.0 when all blocks in a post are version 3 or higher.
  • Enhancement: Public stylesheet now declared via style_handles in block registration, ensuring styles load correctly inside the iframed editor.
  • Fix: Plugin Check warning for interpolated $placeholders in sort-order query suppressed with targeted phpcs:disable/enable — the variable contains only %d tokens and is not user-controlled.
  • Fix: Plugin Check warning for meta_query in pre_get_posts access-control filter suppressed — no alternative API covers this use case.

1.4.9

  • New: Single document page visits now redirect (302) to the download endpoint. This makes the Query Loop block’s “make title a link” option work correctly.
  • New: Documents now appear as a selectable post type in the Core Query Loop block, enabling custom frontend layouts built entirely in the block editor. Public and logged-in access restrictions are enforced at the REST level; role-restricted documents are blocked on individual REST fetches (collection-level role filtering has the same limitation as [trdv_list]).
  • Fix: Expiry dates are now enforced at the download, view, and REST level via can_view_document(). Previously expiry only filtered documents from [trdv_list] output; direct download/view URLs and REST requests could still reach expired documents.
  • Fix: Expired and access-restricted documents are now hidden from the Query Loop block listing entirely. A pre_get_posts hook applies access control and expiry at query level; a the_posts row-level filter removes role-restricted documents that cannot be excluded in SQL.

1.4.8

  • New: Manual sort order — drag the handle column in the admin document list to reorder documents. The first drag establishes positions for all existing documents; subsequent drags update only the visible page. Use [trdv_list orderby="menu_order"] to display documents on the frontend in their manually-defined order.
  • New: Tag support — documents can be tagged via a new flat Tags taxonomy shown as an admin column. Use [trdv_list tag="slug"] to pre-filter by tag and [trdv_list show_tag_filter="true"] for a tag dropdown filter.

1.4.7

  • New: “Include documents in site search” setting — when enabled, documents appear alongside posts and pages in WordPress search results. Access restrictions are respected.
  • New: View button for PDF and image files — opens the file in a new browser tab without forcing a download. Supported in both the [trdv_list] shortcode (show_view="false" to hide) and the DocVault Document block.
  • New: Document description field — set an optional description per document; displayed inline in [trdv_list] with a toggle button, and directly in the DocVault Document block (full layout).
  • New: Clear search button — an × button appears inside the search field when text is entered; clicking it resets the field and refreshes the list.
  • New: Category filter dropdown — [trdv_list show_category_filter="true"] adds a category dropdown alongside the search box.
  • New: File type filter dropdown — [trdv_list show_type_filter="true"] adds a file type dropdown; only types present in the library are listed.
  • New: Download count column — [trdv_list show_count="true"] adds a Downloads column showing total download count per document. Also available as a toggle in the DocVault Document block (full layout).
  • Fixed: Expiry days-remaining calculation now anchors both dates to UTC before comparison, ensuring correct behaviour on servers where the PHP default timezone differs from UTC.

1.4.6

  • Added a description to the Version History metabox explaining that the Restore button makes a previous version the active file served to users.

1.4.5

  • Security: all upload entry points now reject files immediately when content-based MIME validation fails — no fallback to browser-supplied MIME type.
  • Developer: added trdv_allowed_file_types filter to the upload validation, wp_handle_upload() mimes, download tracker MIME check, and upload UI — allows Pro to extend the accepted file type list without patching free plugin code.

1.4.4

  • Fixed: legacy files stored in the old sdm-documents/ directory are now correctly hidden from the media library.
  • Fixed: media library deletion guard now protects legacy sdm-documents/ files, not just the current trdv-documents/ directory.
  • Fixed: storage stats “current vs. old” byte split now uses the explicit current-version pointer rather than assuming the last array entry is current.
  • Fixed: legacy attachment-based files can be deleted through DocVault version management again — the deletion guard was incorrectly blocking the operation.
  • Fixed: replaced deprecated current_time('timestamp', true) calls with time() to eliminate notices on sites with WP_DEBUG enabled.

1.4.3

  • New uploads are no longer registered as WordPress media library attachments — DocVault files are now stored privately and managed entirely within DocVault.
  • Legacy attachment-based files are hidden from the media library grid and modal to prevent accidental deletion.
  • Attempting to delete a DocVault-managed attachment from the media library is now blocked with an explanatory error.
  • Version limit warning replaced with a prominent dismissible banner above the upload area — includes the limit message, a Pro upgrade link, and a “Continue anyway” button. Saving is blocked until the warning is acknowledged or the file is removed.
  • Security: path containment validation added for all path-based file operations (serve and delete) using realpath() to prevent arbitrary file access or deletion if post meta is tampered.
  • Fixed: introduced an explicit current-version pointer (_trdv_current_version_num) so the active file is preserved correctly after a merge operation. Prevents version number collisions and accidental deletion of the current version.

1.4.2

  • Added file type filter dropdown to the admin document list — filter by PDF, DOCX, etc. in one click.
  • Fixed: expiry date hook now fires when the expiry date is cleared, so Pro audit log and email notifications correctly record the change.

1.4.1

  • Added document expiry dates — set an optional expiry date per document; expired documents are hidden from the frontend list automatically. Use [trdv_list show_expired="true"] to include them.
  • Fixed: block renderer and [trdv_link] shortcode now check access control before exposing document metadata
  • Fixed: frontend query applies access-control filtering at query level for anonymous users
  • Fixed: AJAX search reads show_expired from the PHP-rendered data attribute for consistency with initial render; value cannot be set independently via client-side input
  • Fixed: per-document roles access type no longer silently discarded by the save handler
  • Fixed: _trdv_upload_date now uses current_time() WordPress API

1.4.0

  • Added dismissible review notice shown after 21 days on DocVault admin pages
  • Replaced version limit confirm dialog with an inline notice linking to DocVault Pro

1.3.9

  • Fixed download button text being hidden when the theme link colour matches the button background colour

1.3.8

short_description: Document library and manager for WordPress: version history, replace files without breaking links, access control and a searchable document table.
description:
Trilobita DocVault turns WordPress into a document library. Upload a file once and its download link never changes: when you upload a new version, every link on your pages, menus and emails serves the new file automatically. Visitors find documents in a searchable, sortable table, and you keep a version history for every file.

Key Features:

  • Version History – Upload a new version and the download link stays the same. Download, restore or delete earlier versions (up to 5 per document), with optional version notes.
  • Searchable Document Library – The [trdv_list] shortcode shows a responsive table with live search, sortable columns and pagination, plus optional category, tag and file type filters.
  • View in Browser – PDFs get a View button so visitors can read them without downloading.
  • Document List Block – Add a searchable list of documents to any page in the block editor, for example every document in a category (such as the papers for one meeting), and choose the sorting, columns and filters in the block settings.
  • Document Block – Add a single document to any page or post in the block editor, with Full and Minimal layouts.
  • Inline Download Links – Link any text to a document from the block editor toolbar, or with the [trdv_link] shortcode.
  • Access Control – Make documents public or available to logged-in users only, as a site-wide default or per document.
  • Protected Files – Files are served only through DocVault’s download links, which check access first. Direct access to the upload folder is blocked on Apache, and Site Health warns you if your server (for example Nginx) needs a rule.
  • Expiry Dates – Set an optional expiry date and the document is hidden automatically once it passes.
  • Download Tracking – See download counts in the admin list, and optionally show them on the frontend.
  • Drag & Drop Upload – Drop a file to upload it; the title is filled in from the file name.
  • Categories and Tags – Organise documents with their own categories (or share your post categories) and tags.
  • Manual Sort Order – Drag documents into your preferred order and use [trdv_list orderby="menu_order"] to show that order on the frontend.
  • Site Search – Documents appear in your site’s search results (can be turned off).
  • Privacy Tools – Works with the WordPress personal data export and erasure tools.
  • File Types – PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, PPT, PPTX, ODT, ODS, ODP, RTF, CSV and TXT.

If DocVault is useful to you, please consider leaving a review. It helps other people find the plugin.

Switching from another download plugin?

If your site uses WordPress Download Manager or Download Monitor, the free Trilobita DocVault Migrator copies your downloads into DocVault, with a dry run first and rollback if you change your mind. Old download links and shortcodes keep working without editing your pages. WordPress Download Manager and Download Monitor are third-party plugins, not affiliated with Trilobita.

Go further with Trilobita DocVault Pro

Trilobita DocVault Pro adds enterprise-grade features for teams that need more control:

  • Unlimited Version History – Remove the 5-version limit, with optional per-document limits and automatic pruning of old versions.
  • Per-Document Access Control – Restrict individual documents to specific user roles.
  • Audit Trail – Full activity log with CSV export for compliance and accountability.
  • Email Notifications – Configurable alerts for uploads, updates, and approvals.
  • Document Approval Workflow – Require documents to be reviewed before publishing.
  • Bulk Upload – Upload multiple documents at once with duplicate detection.
  • Download Analytics – Detailed per-version download statistics.
  • Duplicate Detection – Find and merge duplicate documents to save storage.
  • Storage Management – Advanced tools for monitoring and cleaning up storage.
  • Card and Button Layouts – Two extra layouts for the Document block.
  • More File Types – Allow images (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP), ZIP, AI and EPS files.
  • Button Colours – Match download buttons to your brand.

Privacy

Trilobita DocVault stores the following user data:

  • Uploader user ID – Stored as post meta (_trdv_uploaded_by) to track who uploaded each document version.
  • Download logs – Each download is recorded with the downloader’s IP address, browser user agent, user ID (if logged in) and the time, in a custom database table (trdv_download_log).

This data is handled in compliance with GDPR and CCPA:

  • The plugin registers with the WordPress privacy tools for data export and erasure requests.
  • Suggested privacy policy text is added to the WordPress Privacy Policy Guide (Settings > Privacy).
  • Download logs for registered users can be exported and erased with the WordPress personal data tools. Downloads by visitors who are not logged in are not linked to an email address, so they cannot be matched by these tools.

Usage

Document Block (Gutenberg):

Add a single document with a download button directly in the block editor:

  1. Click the + button to add a block
  2. Search for “DocVault Document”
  3. Under Select Document, type part of the title and choose the document

Block options:

  • Layout: Full (with icon and download button) or Minimal (compact inline link)
  • Show/hide file icon (full layout only)
  • Show/hide file info (type and size; a file type badge in the minimal layout)
  • Show/hide view button (PDF and images, full layout only)
  • Show/hide description (full layout only)
  • Show/hide download count (full layout only)
  • Alignment (left, center, right, wide)

Document List Block (Gutenberg):

Add a searchable, sortable table of documents in the block editor:

  1. Click the + button to add a block
  2. Search for “DocVault Document List”
  3. In the block settings, choose the categories and tags to list (none selected lists all documents)

Block settings:

  • Documents: categories, tags and file type. Documents in any selected category (including subcategories) that also have any selected tag are listed
  • Sorting: sort by date published, title, manual order, file size, file type or downloads; ascending or descending; documents per page (up to 100)
  • Display: search box, category, tag and file type filters, view and download buttons, download count, and columns
  • Alignment (wide, full)

The block shows the same table as the [trdv_list] shortcode, with the same access control: visitors only see documents they are allowed to access. Categories and tags are saved by ID, so renaming one does not break the block. If every selected category or tag is deleted, the block shows nothing rather than all documents.

[trdv_list] — Document Table Shortcode:

Display a searchable, sortable table of documents on any page or post:

[trdv_list]

Parameters:

  • category – Filter by document category slug, or several slugs separated by commas (documents in any of them)
  • tag – Filter by document tag slug, or several slugs separated by commas (documents in any of them)
  • include – Show only these documents: document IDs separated by commas (up to 100). Combined with the other filters
  • type – Filter by file type (pdf, docx, etc.)
  • orderby – Sort by: date (publish date), title, size, type, downloads, menu_order (default: date). Use menu_order to display documents in the drag-and-drop order set in the admin list. When menu_order is selected and order is not explicitly set, the list defaults to ASC.
  • order – ASC or DESC (default: DESC)
  • show_search – Show search box: true/false (default: true)
  • show_download – Show download button: true/false (default: true)
  • show_view – Show view button for PDFs and images: true/false (default: true)
  • show_category_filter – Show category dropdown filter: true/false (default: false)
  • show_tag_filter – Show tag dropdown filter: true/false (default: false)
  • show_type_filter – Show file type dropdown filter (only types present in the library): true/false (default: false)
  • show_count – Show download count column: true/false (default: false)
  • columns – Columns to display: title, type, size, date (default: title,type,size,date)
  • per_page – Documents per page (default: 20, maximum 100). Use -1 for the maximum
  • show_expired – Include expired documents: true/false (default: false)

Examples:

[trdv_list type="pdf" orderby="title" order="ASC"]
[trdv_list category="reports" show_search="false" columns="title,date"]
[trdv_list orderby="menu_order"]
[trdv_list show_category_filter="true" show_type_filter="true" show_count="true"]
[trdv_list show_tag_filter="true"]
[trdv_list show_download="false" show_view="true"]

Document Link Toolbar Button:

Link any selected text to a document download without leaving the block editor:

  1. Select the text you want to turn into a download link
  2. Click the document icon in the formatting toolbar (“Trilobita DocVault Link”)
  3. Choose a document from the dropdown and click Apply

[trdv_link] — Inline Document Link Shortcode:

Insert a download link within any text:

[trdv_link id="123"]Download the report[/trdv_link]

Parameters:

  • id (required) – The document ID
  • new_tab – Open in new tab: true/false (default: false)
  • class – Add custom CSS class

Examples:

[trdv_link id="123"] - Uses document title as link text
[trdv_link id="123"]Click here[/trdv_link] - Custom link text
[trdv_link id="123" new_tab="true"]Download[/trdv_link] - Opens in new tab

upgrade_notice.1.7.0: Adds the Document List block and a stable order for document lists. Fixes deleting an old version removing a file that a restored version still uses. The Date column in document lists now shows the publish date instead of the latest upload date. If you use DocVault Pro, update it to 1.5.5 as well.
upgrade_notice.1.6.1: Adds an include option to the document list and support for Download Monitor's [downloads] shortcode after migration. No action required on upgrade.
upgrade_notice.1.6.0: Security fixes for documents created without an author and for expiry dates on sites outside UTC, plus compatibility for content migrated from WordPress Download Manager, documents on WordPress category pages, and download history cleanup. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.5.10: Fixes document list search stopping for logged-out visitors on sites that use page caching, and document list sorting (reverse order, Type column, sortable Downloads). Recommended if you use a caching plugin or host-level caching.
upgrade_notice.1.5.9: Security update: restricted and expired documents are no longer shown in site search or on category and tag pages, plus several hardening fixes. Also adds a getting-started guide for new sites. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.5.8: Security fix for the Document block, plus block editor extension points used by DocVault Pro 1.5.4. Update both plugins together if you use Pro.
upgrade_notice.1.5.7: Fixes lost download counts under simultaneous downloads, false expiry change events, and dates shown in UTC instead of your site's time zone.
upgrade_notice.1.5.6: Security update: blocks direct web access to stored document files on Apache, and adds a Site Health check that warns if your server (e.g. Nginx) still allows it. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.5.5: Confirmed compatible with WordPress 7.1. No action required on upgrade.
upgrade_notice.1.5.4: The Document block's document picker now searches all documents via the REST API — the previous 100-document cap is removed. No action required on upgrade.
upgrade_notice.1.5.3: Fixes Download and View button labels wrapping across two lines in the document list.
upgrade_notice.1.5.2: Admin colour scheme compatibility fix — plugin accent colours now track the active admin colour scheme.
upgrade_notice.1.5.0: WordPress 7.0 compatibility update. Block API version updated to 3 for iframed editor support.
upgrade_notice.1.4.9: Adds Core Query Loop block support. Fixes expiry enforcement on direct download/view URLs and REST requests. Expired and access-restricted documents are now hidden from all frontend queries including Query Loop.
upgrade_notice.1.4.8: Adds drag-and-drop manual sort order for the admin document list and a new flat document Tags taxonomy. Use [trdv_list orderby="menu_order"] to apply the custom order on the frontend; use [trdv_list show_tag_filter="true"] for a tag dropdown filter.
upgrade_notice.1.4.7: Adds site search integration, inline document viewer, document descriptions, category and file type filter dropdowns, download count column, and a clear search button. Fixes expiry date timezone handling on non-UTC servers.
upgrade_notice.1.4.6: Minor usability improvement: the Version History metabox now explains what the Restore button does.
upgrade_notice.1.4.5: Developer release: adds the trdv_allowed_file_types filter as an extension point. Required for DocVault Pro 1.4.3+ (configurable additional file types). No behaviour change for free users.
upgrade_notice.1.4.4: Bug fixes for media library hiding and deletion guard on legacy files. Fixes a storage stats calculation issue and removes a deprecated function call. Recommended for all users upgrading from 1.4.3.
upgrade_notice.1.4.3: DocVault files are now stored privately and no longer appear in the media library. Includes a security hardening update for path-based file operations. Recommended update for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.4.2: Adds file type filter to the admin document list and fixes an edge case with expiry date notifications.
upgrade_notice.1.4.1: Adds document expiry dates and includes security fixes for access control in block/shortcode renderers and frontend queries. Recommended update.
upgrade_notice.1.4.0: Adds a review prompt after 21 days and replaces the version limit dialog with an inline Pro upsell notice.
upgrade_notice.1.3.9: Fixes download button text disappearing when the theme link colour matches the button background. Recommended update.
upgrade_notice.1.3.8: Fixes drag-and-drop upload not attaching the file when saving a document. Recommended update for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.3.6: Fixes version history and download log timestamps displaying in the wrong timezone on non-UTC servers.
upgrade_notice.1.3.5: Improved folder structure warning, role-based access upgrade prompt, and help page improvements.
upgrade_notice.1.3.4: Fixes flat folder structure filename prefix after version pruning, download log UTC storage, and adds an admin notice if the uploads directory is not writable on activation.
upgrade_notice.1.3.1: WordPress Plugin Check compliance fixes. Recommended update before WordPress.org submission.
upgrade_notice.1.3.0: Security improvements and WordPress.org compliance. Contains breaking shortcode renames — see changelog.

upgrade_notice.1.2.1: Security hardening and WordPress.org compliance improvements. Recommended update for all users.
